title: SNS: fan out one fact to independent subscribers
outcome: Distinguish publish/subscribe fan-out from competing workers on a queue.
useCase: A ticket event consumed by reporting and notifications.
benefits: Simple fan-out with independently buffered subscribers.
drawbacks: Schema, delivery type, policies, and history/backfill remain explicit choices.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: One queue shares work. Fan-out copies responsibility.

trace.title: Published fact
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

SNS can publish a message to subscriptions. This is fan-out: independent destinations can receive the same published fact.

A set of workers competing on one queue instead shares work among them. Choose based on whether each downstream system needs its own copy.

Use SNS-to-SQS when subscribers need their own buffering and processing pace. Define message schema, subscription filtering, access policies, and failure/retry handling.

Delivery behavior depends on topic and subscription types; record the exact option rather than assuming one global ordering guarantee.

Setup: create a training topic, create a separate queue for each durable subscriber role, add subscriptions/filters, allow only the intended topic to send to each queue, then publish a synthetic event and verify each required subscriber independently.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Publisher sends one fact → SNS evaluates subscriptions/filters → each destination receives according to its delivery contract → each queue/consumer manages its own completion.

One slow subscriber should not dictate another’s progress when their buffers are separate.

Carry an event ID for duplicate handling and traceability. A publish acknowledgement does not prove every subscriber’s business effect completed.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Putting all independent subscribers on one queue makes them compete for messages instead of each receiving all required facts. An overly broad queue policy can allow unintended senders.
